facts.title: Zvartnots
facts.text: Built by Catholicos Nerses III, this circular cathedral was dedicated to Saint Gregory the Illuminator.

facts.title: In 301
facts.text: According to Sebeos, King Tiridates III and Saint Gregory the Illuminator allegedly met at this sacred site.

facts.title: 35.75 meters
facts.text: The building rested on a seven-stepped plinth with this base diameter, rising in three cylindrical tiers.

facts.title: Eagles and baskets
facts.text: The basket capitals displayed Ionic volutes and eagles with spread wings carved into tuff.

facts.title: The 10th century
facts.text: After three hundred and twenty years of existence, a violent earthquake caused the sanctuary to collapse.

facts.title: Toros Toramanian
facts.text: In 1905, the architect drew up his famous three-tiered reconstruction based on the unearthed elements.

facts.title: The church of Ani
facts.text: Around the year 1000, the architect Trdat faithfully reproduced its plan to build the Gagkashen church in Ani.

ytTitle: Zvartnots, the Circular Cathedral of Medieval Armenia
ytLead: Built in the 7th century by Catholicos Nerses III, the circular cathedral of Zvartnots overturned the canons of Armenian medieval architecture before collapsing in the 10th century.
